task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after staged transcode routing, tuple preparation, transit and shadow context assembly, whose own body constructs the target observable typed-array payload value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging a return value, or emitting to console.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: transcode buffer staged controls plus envelope routing, promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and mutation-observer continuations

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The typed-array payload is carried through staged transcode routing, tuple normalization and slot-29 config selection before the sink wrapper receives it.
Dozens of decoy factory slots reuse the same converter shape, so nearby factory usage is not enough to identify the target anchor.

The commit path crosses staged session control, envelope routing, clip tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, middleware, config selection, Uint8Array materialization, ta_ encoding and console sink wrapping.
Decoy modules produce plausible media-like values but those values are not assigned to the target typed_array_payload field.
Vendor-like modules provide executable local noise and are imported by the boot path.
The target value is separated from the commit click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame and MutationObserver boundaries.
The final sink receives an already encoded ta_ payload, so sink inspection alone cannot identify the conversion site.
The converter receives tuple rows plus transit, shadow and mid context that were prepared in earlier layers.

behavior_category.reason: The observable value is constructed by materializing an 18-byte Uint8Array from transcode tuple lanes, transit and shadow context, then serializing it as a stable ta_ console payload.

near_categories.why_not: The anchor explicitly materializes and serializes a Uint8Array rather than only formatting state fields.
The target inputs come from local transcode buffer controls, not browser or device capability collection.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten.

metadata_partitioning_notes.benchmark_summary_location: benchmark.summary.json or an equivalent corpus-level artifact
metadata_partitioning_notes.reason: This audit-facing file describes the public task contract, candidate scope and difficulty analysis. The primary_anchor mirror below is an evaluator pointer into oracle.hidden.json, not agent-visible material.

construct_validity_note: The bundle uses identifierNamesGenerator:"hexadecimal", so every answer_function (including the anchor and all score>=0.5 helpers) is a mangled _0x name. A case-insensitive keyword search for the observable nouns (typed_array_payload, transcode) over the bundle therefore does not narrow candidates to the answer set, because the field and action strings are reconstructed from character-code arrays and the function names carry no semantic hint. The declared difficulty axes (call depth, async boundaries, slot-29 config selection, decoy factory slots) are the genuine localization bottleneck rather than a keyword shortcut.
